title: Prince Rupert to William Legge, letters in code (Dartmouth papers)
correspondents: Prince Rupert to William Legge (also Digby to Legge)
folio_note: 12 items: I/i/37, I/i/39, I/i/45, I/i/48, I/i/46, I/i/47, I/i/49, I/i/53, I/i/54, I/i/55, I/i/56, I/i/59. One on linen (53). Two noted 'not deciphered' (56 Digby, 59 Rupert); 49 'in code, without translation'
status: Staffordshire catalogue: 'in code', several not deciphered. Rupert / Charles I ciphers read by Lasry (SP106-3/5 keys) may apply. Not on DECODE (known.py: no hit). Checked 28 Oct 2026: Not opened in detail (Discovery pages did not render in WebFetch). Search found no decipherment; Warburton (1849) prints some Rupert-Legge letters and should be grepped before ordering images. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. Eliot Warburton, Memoirs of Prince Rupert and the Cavaliers (1849), 3 vols, Rupert-Legge letters 'from the Earl of Dartmouth's MSS': vol. II pp. 406-408 (April 1644, flagged 'In Cipher', Master of the Horse; letters of 18 and 23 Apr 1644); vol. III pp. 27-28 (Oct 1644, flagged '[In cipher]'); pp. 63-64 and 69-70 (March 1645); pp. 73-74 (Hereford, 31 Mar 1645); p. 100 (Daventry, 8 June 1645); pp. 125-128 (Digby to Legge, answering Legge's of 22 June; Legge's reply, pp. 128-131, cites Digby's letter of 30 June 1645); pp. 151-156 (Bristol, 28-29 July 1645). Staffordshire item dates from the TNA Discovery API (28 Oct 2026): /37 = 30 Apr 1644 (Master of the Horse; matches Warburton II 406-408, whose letters are dated 18 and 23 Apr, so date mismatch), /39 = 10 Oct 1644 (Warburton III 27-28), /41 = 8 Mar 1645 (III 63-64, matched on content), /45 = 31 Mar 1645 (III 73-74, exact date), /54 = 8 June 1645 (III p.100, exact), /56 = Digby 30 June 1645 (III 125-128, printed in full as plain text; the 'coded part not deciphered' is therefore deciphered in print). So six of the twelve items are printed in 1849 with plaintext. Warburton leaves Rupert's own name and some name-cipher groups as '[cipher]' or bare numbers (e.g. '92, 352' in the 29 July 1645 letter, III p.156) and says (II p.471 fn) that he gives uninterpreted ciphers only where he cannot read them. Not located in Warburton: /46 /47 /48 /49 /53 /55 (dates not retrieved) and /59 (Rupert, 9 Aug 1645, 'not deciphered'; the last printed Rupert-Legge letter is 29 July 1645). HMC Dartmouth (1887) calendars only Rupert-Legge letters of 1661. Verdict: lead is mostly closed for 37/39/41/45/54/56; items 59 and probably 46-49, 53, 55 remain unprinted, and the printed ones give plaintext cribs for the Rupert-Legge key.
why: Rupert's private letters to the Legge circle in the 1644-45 court quarrels, in his own cipher.
